newsitem.title: FRANCE: ONIC head sees no incentive for Africa wheat sales.
newsitem.headline: ONIC head sees no incentive for Africa wheat sales.

text.p: The head of France's grain office ONIC said on Wednesday that exporters who applied for long-term licences to sell EU wheat to a target group of African nations had no incentive to show proof of contract by the November 15 deadline.
ONIC director general Alain Moulinier explained that regular EU wheat export refunds now exceeded the special refunds applying to wheat exports to these nations.
Under the so-called article 9 traders must show proof of sale to get the refund for the long-term licences they applied for. They have until 1400 GMT on November 15 to do so.
Licences carry a special refund of 12 Ecus per tonne until December and 19 Ecus from December onwards. The licences are valid until June 30, 1996.
When the EU set the special refunds, world wheat prices were still firm. But since then the EU stepped up its refund on wheat exports to keep pace with falling world prices.

"The special refund has become non-operational. It is not very likely that contracts corresponding to the demand for long-term licences will be submitted," Moulinier told a regular monthly news conference.
Under the long-term scheme traders have applied for licences to export between 350,00 tonnes to one million tonnes of wheat, Moulinier said.
Moulinier said a rise in the special refund for Africa could not be ruled out but said much hinged on world price fluctuations and on the level of the regular EU rebate for wheat exports.
"The Commission may give it some thought if no contracts are submitted," he said --Paris newsroom +331 4221 5432
